subject: Elkwood: Discovery recap — PII handling, retention & audit criteria
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@elkwoodfinance.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — PII handling, retention & audit criteria

Jordan / Sara — thanks again for the time today. Below is a concise recap of the discussion and the technical asks we captured. Please flag anything missing or incorrect.

Key pain points you shared:
- Risk of sensitive customer data (SSNs, bank account numbers) being stored in third-party inference logs and exposed during audits.
- Inability to demonstrate per-request audit trails for regulated customers.
- Current latency/cost concerns limiting use of LLM features in core workflows (esp. batch reconciliations).

Current stack notes (from your team):
- Primary app: Java microservices on AWS (us-west-2), customer data in RDS (PII in separate schema).
- Tokenization and pre-processing performed in-house; requests to model are routed through an API gateway.
- Logging: centralized ELK stack with 60-day retention by default; security team requires 7-year retention for auditable events for accounts flagged as regulated.

Success criteria you listed:
1) No customer-identifiable PII stored in inference logs by default (we discussed token redaction and on-device/edge pre-processing options).
2) Ability to produce a tamper-evident audit trail for each request tied to an internal request id and customer tenant id.
3) Configurable retention windows per-tenant (e.g., 90 days for non-regulated, 7+ years for regulated).
4) Cryptographic key control for any encrypted logs (bring-your-own-key/KMS).

Security & compliance constraints called out:
- PII types in scope: SSN, bank routing/account numbers, full card PAN, DOB when combined with account numbers.
- Need for deterministic hashing option (salted per-tenant) for searchable identifiers without storing raw values.
- Audit logs must include: timestamp, request id, model name+version, route, redaction/hash metadata, and a link to the original request record (or internal ID).
- Retention policy must be configurable per-tenant with legal hold capability.
- Evidence requested for SOC 2 and encryption-at-rest/in-transit; your procurement will request these artifacts during contract review.

Immediate next steps (agreed):
- We will share (by EOD Monday) a short template: minimal data schema + example payloads with PII flagged and suggested redaction/hash transforms. Attachment: elkwood_data_inventory.xlsx (sample inventory).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive between Elkwood security + Redwood platform engineers (45–60m). Action owner: Marcus. Proposed slots: Tue/Wed next week (I sent a Doodle).
- Provide a short note on logging controls we can enforce at the routing layer (log masking, token exclusion, per-tenant retention) and an outline of the audit export format. Action owner: Neha.

Proposed timeline: technical deep-dive this week, MAP (mutual action plan) and rough SOW draft by end of next week, procurement kickoff the following week.

Attachments: elkwood_data_inventory.xlsx (summary you provided) — we'll use this to map PII fields to masking rules.

Thanks again — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@elkwoodfinance.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@elkwoodfinance.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — PII handling, retention & audit criteria

Marcus — thanks for the recap, this looks accurate. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) Retention: the 7-year retention is a hard requirement for a subset of our enterprise tenants (we call these "regulated"). For other tenants we can keep 90 days. Legal hold will be required in case of subpoenas.

2) Deterministic hashing: we need deterministic, tenant-scoped hashing so we can correlate events for the same individual without storing PII.

3) Audit exports: the compliance team wants a signed export (digest) mechanism for audit batches — basically we need to show integrity of exported logs.

Next steps from our side: I'll share a redacted sample payload by EOD today. Also looping in Sara (security lead) to coordinate the engineering deep-dive. Please include your infra/security engineer if possible.

-Jordan
Jordan Mills
Head of Product Security, Elkwood Financial
jordan.mills@elkwoodfinance.com | +1 (206) 777-1212
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@elkwoodfinance.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — PII handling, retention & audit criteria

Jordan — great notes. Quick engineering-level confirmation on a few points so we align for the deep-dive: 

- Deterministic per-tenant hashing: supported. We can provide a library or in-line transform that uses tenant-scoped salt stored in your KMS. Hashes are reproducible and search-friendly; raw PII can be excluded from logs.
- Redaction at ingestion: we support configurable redaction filters (regex + field-map) and an option to never persist raw tokens from configured fields.
- Audit export integrity: we can sign exports with a customer-managed key (HMAC using tenant KMS key) and include export digests in the audit manifest.
- Retention & legal hold: retention windows are per-tenant. Legal hold will suspend deletion; holdings are visible in admin console.

I'll prepare a short one-pager that outlines these controls and a sample audit export format before the deep-dive. Marcus — I included a stub of the export JSON format in the wiki link below.

Related: https://redwood.app/docs/security/audit-export-samples

Neha Kapoor
Product Security, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@elkwoodfinance.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — PII handling, retention & audit criteria

Thanks — this is helpful. Two quick asks before the deep-dive: 

1) Can you include an example of a redaction policy applied to our sample payload (we'll send that payload in ~2 hours)? If you can show pre- and post-redaction, that would be ideal.
2) Procurement will want high-level pricing sensitivity for log retention tiers (90 days vs 7 years) — can you provide an order-of-magnitude delta so we can budget?

If those are doable, we'll lock the deep-dive time this afternoon (we proposed 3:30pm PT).

Sara Bloom
